markdown_report:
### Evidence and directions

Three baseline insights guide this first experiment. (1) Electronics has 10.71% sampled ranking errors and a −0.0749 tenth-percentile margin. This motivates improving difficult candidate discrimination without assuming its cause. (2) Embedding-collapse scores near 0.5 imply approximately zero mean cosine similarity. Collapse regularization therefore lacks diagnostic support. (3) Users reject broad associations, redundant alternatives, and compatibility mismatches. Ordered interactions provide supervision, but do not label compatibility or completed needs.

Three literature insights narrow the options. (1) HSTU supports causal sequence modeling with temporal biases [1]. Temporal extensions are feasible, but recency alone cannot identify purchase completion. (2) HSTU-BLaIR integrates content inside one network [2]. Its external pretrained encoder is prohibited here, so scratch-trained content remains an unverified adaptation. (3) HSTU’s reference configuration uses multiple sampled negatives [3]. False-negative research cautions that aggressive mining can suppress relevant items [4].

### Framework and candidate assessment

The framework separates **representation** (specific item attributes), **context** (current intent), and **competition** (discriminating plausible alternatives). All candidates retain one HSTU per category. Scores are originality/potential/user alignment/model alignment/difficulty; higher difficulty means harder implementation.

| Candidate | Scores | Positive assessment | Negative assessment |
|---|---|---|---|
| Scratch title/description residual embeddings [2] | 5/7/8/6/6 | Adds observable distinctions within one network | Sparse supervision may not learn technical semantics |
| Elapsed-time attention bias [1] | 3/6/7/4/4 | Conditions relevance on recent activity | Cannot establish satisfied needs |
| **Lexically guided moderate-negative curriculum** [3,4] | **4/7/7/8/3** | Targets confusing alternatives with minimal backbone changes | Similar unseen items may be valid future choices |

These assessments are hypotheses, not measured improvements. The selected curriculum fits 0% research progress because it changes only training competition and is inexpensive to ablate.

### Selected experiment

Build lexical neighbor lists from training-visible titles and descriptions using TF–IDF, without pretrained weights or unavailable attributes. Retain model numbers, units, and format tokens. Train the corrected HSTU with 32 negatives per valid next-item position: initially uniform; gradually replace eight with moderately scored lexical neighbors. Draw neighbors of the observed positive, exclude known training interactions, and retain uniform fallback. Detach scores used for selection.

This explicitly targets two user failures: broad thematic matches displacing specific choices, and redundant alternatives occupying top positions. Distinguishing similar alternatives may also help format mismatches, but cannot certify compatibility. Quantitatively, it targets Electronics’ weak lower-tail margins.

```
pool = lexical_neighbors(positive) minus known_training_items
hard = middle_upper_score_quantile(HSTU(context), pool)
negatives = uniform(32 - scheduled_k) + sample(hard, scheduled_k)
loss = cross_entropy([positive_score, negative_scores], target=0)
```

Use uncorrected candidate-set cross-entropy; do not claim an unbiased full-softmax estimator. Preserve seeds, four-category routing, final nonpadding readout, and diagnostic interfaces. Select solely by pinned macro validation HR@10; compare uniform-only training under equal update budgets. Lexical lists are training artifacts, never inference scores.

References: [1] HSTU, arXiv:2402.17152. [2] HSTU-BLaIR, KDD workshop 2025. [3] Official HSTU sampled-softmax configuration. [4] arXiv:2208.04116.

idea.description: Retain the corrected HSTU architecture and introduce a curriculum mixing uniform negatives with moderately difficult lexical neighbors of each training positive. Each category has one independently trained model and one selected checkpoint.
idea.motivation: The user diagnosis identifies broad associations and redundant alternatives at the top of recommendations. Training against plausible, similar alternatives may improve discrimination between these items and the observed next choice. Electronics provides the strongest quantitative motivation: 10.71% negative-over-positive errors and a negative tenth-percentile margin. These observations motivate an experiment; they do not establish that negative sampling caused the failures.
idea.implementation_notes: Use only permitted titles and descriptions to construct training-only TF–IDF neighbor lists. Preserve meaningful alphanumeric model identifiers, measurements, and format tokens; cap vocabulary and neighbor count to bound CPU memory. Do not use item categories, ratings, prices, stores, reviews, external datasets, or pretrained weights. Sample 32 unique negatives excluding padding, the positive, and the user's known training interactions; use uniform fallback when lexical pools are insufficient. Ramp lexical negatives from zero to eight over the first 20% of the configured training horizon. Select from the detached-score 50th–80th percentile of eligible lexical candidates, avoiding exclusively highest-score mining. These settings are proposed starting values, not validated optima. Use candidate-set cross-entropy without unjustified logQ correction. Preserve preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, at most 200 epochs, and 200 batches per epoch. DATA_DIR remains os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR']; store artifacts beneath the trial directory. Keep the supplied HSTU scoring and predictor architecture identical, so working/predict.py loads only the selected category checkpoint and performs no lexical reranking. Preserve ModelView, sample_batch, item_emb, log2feats(sequence), and predict_score(features, items). DiagnosisProbe(view, device).run_full_diagnosis(train_loader) must return measured metrics and metric_definitions; diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis) must use those measurements and definitions. Existing margin probes can continue using their supplied negatives; record sampled-negative distributions when comparing diagnostics. Empty metadata-category breakdowns must remain unavailable rather than populated with inferred categories. Use final nonpadding indices for left-padded histories. Compare the curriculum against uniform-only multi-negative training to isolate mining effects, within the shared GPU budget. No performance improvement is claimed before host validation.
idea.pseudocode:
For each category, initialize the supplied corrected HSTU with seed 42.
Build sparse lexical neighbor lists from permitted item titles/descriptions.
For epoch in the configured horizon, capped at 200:
    k = ramp_from_zero_to_eight(epoch)
    For each of exactly 200 training batches:
        Obtain the family-specific (sequence, positive, negative) batch.
        features = model.log2feats(sequence)
        For each valid target position, using chunked/vectorized operations:
            eligible = lexical_neighbors[positive] excluding padding, positive, and known training interactions
            With gradients disabled, score eligible candidates using the same model.
            Choose up to k unique candidates from score quantiles [0.50, 0.80].
            Fill the remaining slots with unique uniform eligible negatives, to 32 where feasible.
        Compute positive and negative logits with the existing HSTU scorer.
        loss = mean cross_entropy(concat(positive_logits, negative_logits), zero_target)
        Backpropagate through the selected logits and update the single model.
    Evaluate only through the unchanged permitted validation process.
Select by macro validation HR@10 and serialize one checkpoint per category.
Write the baseline-compatible predictor with the same architecture/configuration.
At inference, route category, read the final nonpadding feature, and score candidates using that checkpoint alone.

originality.positive: Combines lexical proximity and moderate same-model difficulty in a small, constraint-compatible HSTU sampling change.
originality.negative: Content-guided hard-negative sampling and curricula are established techniques; this is an adaptation rather than a new model class.

future_potential.positive: Offers a controlled route to investigate whether training competition improves specific next-item discrimination across heterogeneous categories.
future_potential.negative: Unobserved relevance and sparse metadata can make lexical neighbors misleading; better training margins may not improve held-out HR@10.

code_difficulty.positive: Changes sampling and loss while preserving the supplied backbone, diagnostic scoring interfaces, and inference architecture.
code_difficulty.negative: Efficient filtering, detached candidate scoring, and chunking require care to avoid excessive training cost and false negatives.

related_work.title: Actions Speak Louder than Words: Trillion-Parameter Sequential Transducers for Generative Recommendations
contributions: Introduces the HSTU sequential recommendation backbone.
Provides temporal and positional mechanisms compatible with causal sequence modeling.
limitations: Does not establish optimal settings for the four supplied Amazon categories.
Temporal relevance does not directly identify completed purchase needs.

related_work.title: HSTU-BLaIR
contributions: Integrates projected content embeddings with item-ID representations before HSTU encoding.
limitations: Uses externally pretrained BLaIR representations, which are prohibited in this task.
Does not validate the proposed scratch-trained content alternative.

related_work.title: Official HSTU sampled-softmax reference configuration
contributions: Supplies a concrete HSTU configuration using multiple negatives and normalized representations.
limitations: MovieLens configuration values are not demonstrated optima for this benchmark.
Does not validate lexical mining or the proposed curriculum.

related_work.title: False-negative research cited in the supplied search results
contributions: Motivates caution when treating difficult unobserved items as negative examples.
limitations: Does not establish the false-negative rate of the supplied Amazon splits.
Does not validate the proposed lexical quantile thresholds.
